review_notes: Read the whole file, the Yosida approximation simp lemmas (yosidaOperator_zero is simp), and the downstream uses in Generation.lean and ExponentialComparison.lean. The simp-tagged lemmas (naturalShift_coe, yosidaStrongLimit_zero) look correctly oriented and non-looping. The only interface gap I found is the missing unfolding lemma for yosidaOperatorSequence. It is minor, and I did not run Lean.

findings.problem: The new definition has no companion unfolding lemma such as an `_apply` equation for `yosidaOperatorSequence t n`. Its only simp interface is to unfold the definition by name in each `simpa only [yosidaOperatorSequence, ...]`; yosidaStrongLimit_add does this at line 174. Nothing normalises `R.yosidaOperatorSequence t n` to `R.yosidaOperator (naturalShift n) t`. That matters because the other simp lemmas (`yosidaOperator_zero`, `yosidaOperator_add`) are stated for `yosidaOperator`. The sequence also appears as an argument to `strongOperatorLimit`, so a plain `simp` cannot see the operator-level lemmas through it.
findings.proposed_change: Add `theorem yosidaOperatorSequence_apply (R : ContractiveResolvent E) (t : NNReal) (n : ℕ) : R.yosidaOperatorSequence t n = R.yosidaOperator (naturalShift n) t := rfl` and mark it `@[simp]`. The direction is safe: the right side is built from the `yosidaOperator` constants that the existing simp lemmas target, so it cannot cycle. Then use it in `yosidaStrongLimit_add` instead of unfolding by name. Alternatively, make the sequence `@[reducible]` or `abbrev`.
findings.benefit: Proofs about the sequence would reach the existing `yosidaOperator_zero` and `yosidaOperator_add` simp rules directly, without `simpa only [yosidaOperatorSequence, ...]`. Later files that use the sequence would also get a canonical normal form.
